# A job configuration whose file Close did not settle (MODEL: the loader
# returns ec2job.LoadConfig's unsettled error, holding a model owner, not
# a file) fails the command before any EC2 call, session or job request,
# and before any journal exists. The command keeps the error, with its
# owner, across a later successful command.

skygo-ec2 start -config $CONFIG -state $STATE -credentials $CREDS -interval 0
code 0

configunsettled
ec2mark
! job run -job $WORK/job -task $WORK/task.json -workdir $WORK/src
code 1
stderr 'close of the configuration file did not settle'
! stderr 'keeping the job directory locked'
! stdout .
ec2since 0
opens 0
unsettled 1
keptconfig 1
calls BeginArtifactUpload 0
jobs 0
! exists $WORK/job

# Another job's command succeeds; the first command keeps its owner.
job run -job $WORK/other -task $WORK/task.json -workdir $WORK/src -poll 100ms
code 0
stdout '"state": "SUCCEEDED"'
unsettled 1
keptconfig 1
opens 1
jobs 1

# The same failure for a command on an existing journal opens neither
# the journal nor a session, and the command keeps its own owner.
configunsettled
ec2mark
! job resume -job $WORK/other
code 1
stderr 'close of the configuration file did not settle'
ec2since 0
opens 1
unsettled 2
keptconfig 2
calls SubmitWorkspaceJob 1

# The journal was never opened by the refused command, so it is free.
job job-status -job $WORK/other
code 0
stdout '"state": "SUCCEEDED"'
unsettled 2
opens 2

# The MODEL owners hold no file, so the script settles them.
release
unsettled 0

mutations 1

-- task.json --
{"argv":["/bin/true"],"timeoutSeconds":"60"}
-- src/input.txt --
input
